Page: Kazuo Ishiguro. Sentence: Kazuo Ishiguro OBE, FRSA, FRSL (Japanese: カズオ・イシグロ or 石黒 一雄 ; born 8 November 1954) is a British novelist, screenwriter and short story writer.
Page: Kazuo Ishiguro. Sentence: He was born in Nagasaki, Japan; his family moved to England in 1960 when he was five.
Page: Kazuo Ishiguro. Sentence: Ishiguro obtained his bachelor's degree from the University of Kent in 1978 and his Master's from the University of East Anglia's creative writing course in 1980.
Page: Yukio Mishima. Sentence: Yukio Mishima (三島 由紀夫 , Mishima Yukio ) is the pen name of Kimitake Hiraoka (平岡 公威 , Hiraoka Kimitake , January 14, 1925November 25, 1970) , a Japanese author, poet, playwright, actor, and film director.
Page: Yukio Mishima. Sentence: Mishima is considered one of the most important Japanese authors of the 20th century.
Page: Yukio Mishima. Sentence: He was considered for the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1968 but the award went to his countryman Yasunari Kawabata.
Page: Yukio Mishima. Sentence: His works include the novels "Confessions of a Mask" and "The Temple of the Golden Pavilion", and the autobiographical essay "Sun and Steel".
Page: Yukio Mishima. Sentence: His avant-garde work displayed a blending of modern and traditional aesthetics that broke cultural boundaries, with a focus on sexuality, death, and political change.
Page: Yukio Mishima. Sentence: Mishima was active as a nationalist and founded his own right-wing militia, the Tatenokai.
Page: Yukio Mishima. Sentence: In 1970, he and three other members of his militia staged an attempted "coup d'état" when they seized control of a Japanese military base and took the commander hostage, then tried and failed to inspire a coup to restore the Emperor's pre-war powers.
Page: Yukio Mishima. Sentence: Mishima then committed ritual suicide by "seppuku".
Page: Yukio Mishima. Sentence: The coup attempt became known as the "Mishima Incident".
Page: When We Were Orphans. Sentence: When We Were Orphans is the fifth novel by the British-Japanese author Kazuo Ishiguro, published in 2000.

Facts:
- Yukio Mishima was the pen name of Kimitake Hiraoka, a Japanese author, poet, playwright, actor, and film director born on January 14, 1925.
- Kazuo Ishiguro was born on 8 November 1954 in Nagasaki, Japan.
- Kazuo Ishiguro's family moved to England in 1960 when he was five.
- Yukio Mishima was considered one of the most important Japanese authors of the 20th century.
- Yukio Mishima was considered for the 1968 Nobel Prize in Literature, but Yasunari Kawabata received the award.
- In 1970, Yukio Mishima and three members of Tatenokai seized a Japanese military base, took the commander hostage, and unsuccessfully tried to incite a coup to restore the Emperor's pre-war powers.
- The failed 1970 coup attempt became known as the Mishima Incident.
- After the failed coup attempt in 1970, Yukio Mishima committed ritual suicide by seppuku.
- Kazuo Ishiguro received a bachelor's degree from the University of Kent in 1978.
- Kazuo Ishiguro received a master's degree from the University of East Anglia's creative writing course in 1980.
- Kazuo Ishiguro is a British novelist, screenwriter, and short story writer.
- Kazuo Ishiguro holds the honors OBE, FRSA, and FRSL.
- Yukio Mishima's works include the novels Confessions of a Mask and The Temple of the Golden Pavilion and the autobiographical essay Sun and Steel.
- Yukio Mishima's avant-garde work blended modern and traditional aesthetics and focused on sexuality, death, and political change.
- Yukio Mishima was active as a nationalist and founded the right-wing militia Tatenokai.
- When We Were Orphans is the fifth novel by British-Japanese author Kazuo Ishiguro and was published in 2000.
